latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




The People’s Republic of China (PRC) and Central Asian countries are now focusing on Iran as an additional trade route between Asia and Europe, reflecting the PRC’s ambition to have multiple paths so none can be blocked and its confidence that trade volume will grow.



Central Asian countries are going along with this shift from an “either/or” to a “both/and” approach both because they too increasingly recognize the risks of relying on one path alone and because the PRC is paying for most of the necessary transportation infrastructure.



Such a shift, however, changes the geopolitics of much more than Central Asia, affecting the role of Russia and the South Caucasus as transit routes and powers such as Türkiye, the European Union, and the United States, which have bet on the development of a single route.
